question: Round 1 (discovery, 2-lens fan-out) returned VERIFIED from both lenses with zero Critical/Major and eight nits across the two artifacts. Two nits were factual errors in records this session wrote (a wrong test count and a missing sessionNumber in test-runs.jsonl) and were fixed. Three substantive nits remain: (a) a backstop attempt that fails in transport is never ledgered, (b) round NUMBERING still comes from artifacts on disk rather than the ledger, so losing artifacts could duplicate a round number, and (c) the new refusal message interpolates the set dir into a copy-pasteable command without quoting, so a repo path containing spaces yields a broken command. Fix them now, or record them as adjudicated-minor and close?
decision: Record all three as adjudicated-minor residuals and close. (a) is correct as designed and matches verify_session: only a round that produced a verdict consumes budget, and a failed billable attempt is still audited in router-metrics.jsonl. (b) is pre-existing Set 111 S1 behaviour that this session did not introduce or worsen; the claim it strains is a wording one (the ledger is the true count of rounds RUN, not the allocator of round numbers). (c) is a real if small usability bug, and it is a pre-existing CLASS -- verify_session's own refusal message and gate_checks._verify_session_command interpolate the same path unquoted -- so fixing only the site I added would leave the class alive and misrepresent it as closed (L-069-1). Named as a deferred residual with the sibling sites listed instead.

options.consequence: Follows the constitution's explicit Minor-only rule -- a Minor-only round is effectively VERIFIED, record the nits and proceed -- and the operator's own severity-gated-stop rule from Set 086. Costs one named residual carried into a follow-on. Risk: the quoting bug reaches an operator with a spaced repo path before the follow-on lands, where it degrades a copy-pasteable command into one needing manual quoting.

options.option: Fix the quoting bug at the site this session added
options.consequence: Cheap in code, but stales the just-passed verification stamp and buys a fresh metered round for a nit -- exactly the grinding this set exists to end -- and leaves the two pre-existing sibling sites unfixed while the changelog would read as though the class were closed.

options.option: Fix the whole quoting class across all three sites
options.consequence: Closes the class honestly, but expands scope beyond this session's plan mid-close, touches a file (gate_checks) already outside the spec's Touches list, and still costs a re-verification round. Better as a small scoped follow-on where its own tests can plant a spaced path.

question: Reduce the close-out gate set per the operator's 2026-08-10 ruling: keep verification_integrity, uat_walk_recorded and test_run_fresh as blocking gates; keep working_tree_clean and pushed_to_remote as transactional preconditions; demote checklist_posted, activity_log_entry, next_orchestrator_present, change_log_fresh and verification_method_vocabulary to warn-not-block; delete nothing. This is a verification reduction and cannot be self-authorized. Does the ruling still stand, given that verification_method_vocabulary turns out to be the only close-time enforcement of a legal verification_method token?
decision: Operator re-attested the ruling AS WRITTEN, with all five demotions including verification_method_vocabulary, after being shown the token-hygiene consequence. Implementation: a demoted check still runs, still prints, and keeps its tests -- only its veto is removed. Nothing is deleted.

options.consequence: Ten checks become three gates plus two preconditions plus five printed-but-non-blocking signals. The substance of the Set 083 bypass incident is still refused, by the EVIDENCE layer of verification_integrity, which this change does not touch. Residual accepted: a corroborated close (or any --manual-verify close) can now persist an illegal verification_method token into session-state.json and the events ledger, because validate_disposition's rule 4 is not run at close and the vocabulary check was its only close-time enforcement point. Data hygiene, not a verification hole.

Four demotions instead of five; no close can ever persist an illegal token. Costs the coherence of the operator's own table (three-plus-one rather than three) and leaves a spelling check holding a veto -- the precise thing the ruling characterises as ceremony.
Nothing is journaled and nothing ships. Sessions 1 and 2 stay closed and pushed; Session 3 stays registered and in-flight, resumable from the same point.

question: The required end-of-set path-aware critique split. gemini-2.5-pro returned VERIFIED ('the documentation has been updated to be consistent with all code changes'); gpt-5.4 raised ONE Major/contract-drift claiming close-out.md's attested-override bullet is false on the actual close path. That bullet says the method-vocabulary check is advisory there, so it warns rather than refuses, and such a close can persist a retired token. Accept the finding, dismiss it, rewrite the docs as asked, or get a third-provider opinion?
decision: Operator dismissed the Major as a false positive AND directed the one real grain be fixed. The doc statement is TRUE and a passing regression test asserts exactly it: the test closes the real Set 083 incident disposition on the attested-override path and asserts result=succeeded, vocab.passed=False, vocab.blocking=False. On that path the close backstop is skipped, verification_integrity is excused by the attestation, and every other predicate -- including the new vocabulary row -- still runs and warns. The critic's own text concedes this ('the only real on-disk behavior change ... is the later advisory gate row') before labelling the doc that says so false. THE GRAIN THAT IS REAL: the close backstop's own refusal message read '(or close with the attested override, which the operator's ruling now lets through with a warning)', which a careful reader could take as describing the backstop path. Reworded to state explicitly that the attested override is a separate invocation which never reaches the backstop at all. PHRASING NOTE: this entry names the attested-override flag in prose rather than as a literal, because the journal's keyword screen matches the literal; the entry is at human authority with a full attestation either way.

options.option: Dismiss the Major as factually wrong AND clarify the backstop message (chosen)
options.consequence: Records the dismissal with an executable citation rather than an opinion, and removes the ambiguity that produced the finding so a later reviewer does not raise it again. Costs a ~5-minute pytest re-run to refresh the run-of-record digest; no extra routed round, because the evidence stamp was already stale from the round-1 nit fixes and a bounded backstop round was coming regardless.
Cheapest; closes immediately. Leaves wording a careful reader can misread, so the same finding is likely to recur.

options.option: Accept the Major and rewrite close-out.md as the critic asks
options.consequence: Closes the finding without argument, but makes the documentation LESS accurate: it removes a true statement that a passing test asserts, leaving operators less informed about what the attested override actually does with an illegal token.

An independent tiebreak where the two critics split cleanly. Costs a routed call and several minutes; the dispute is settleable by running one existing test, which is stronger evidence than a third model's reading.

operator_attestation: Operator, 2026-08-10, education-mode brief via AskUserQuestion presenting the finding verbatim, the dismissal reason, the contradicting test, the context both critics saw, and a stated self-assessment of high confidence: 'Dismiss + clarify the message (Recommended)'.
